gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a 230 V window AC, the 18,000 BTU class sold as 230 V-only (Midea MAW18S2WWT: 230 V, 10 A), needs a 240 V station. Of the stations on our page, Anker's own page shows 240 V only on the SOLIX F3800, which delivers it through a NEMA 14-50 and an L14-30 outlet (6,000 W max at 240 V) and has no NEMA 6-15 or 6-20 receptacle.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages, buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/window-ac/ and generatorchecker.com/guides/window-ac-on-power-station/, and the top result, stationhours.com/best-power-station-for-window-ac/. None of them mentions 230 V or 240 V window ACs, NEMA 6-15 or 6-20 plugs, or which station outlets deliver 240 V. BuyerSheet assumes a 115 V 8,000 BTU unit. GeneratorChecker covers 115 V Midea and Frigidaire 8,000 BTU units and a soft starter. GeneratorChecker already says BLUETTI Power Lifting is for resistive loads only (AC200L) and that Anker SurgePad works best with heating devices, so the mode-exclusion point is taken. That is why I put 240 V as the best finding.
decides: For the usual 5,000 to 8,000 BTU 115 V unit, this changes nothing and the 2 kWh picks stand. For a shopper with a 230 V window unit (18,000 BTU class), it decides the pick. Of the stations on our page, only the Anker SOLIX F3800 (or F3800 Plus) has a 240 V outlet on its maker page, and the shopper still needs a cord or adapter from the 14-50R or L14-30R outlet to the AC's 6-15P or 6-20P plug. The page should carry a line like 'check the voltage on your AC's nameplate; 230 V units need a 240 V station'.

unsourced: The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 and Elite 300 ECO mode (AC output auto-off): its default state, watt threshold and timer. The maker PDFs at s4.bluettipower.com would not extract (compressed binary) and the manuals.plus mirrors returned 403. Only a review (autoevolution) and forum posts say it is on by default, so I left it out. It matters because a cycling window AC in energy-saver mode draws very little between cycles, and ECO mode could cut the outlet if that low draw lasts past the timer.
